title: My reflection stopped copying me 🪞
style_prompt: cinematic horror film still, dark moody blue-teal grade, one bright light source, well exposed, 35mm film grain, realistic, no text, no watermark, no faces
hook_text: At 4:12 a.m. my reflection stopped copying me.

scenes.narration: At 4:12 a.m. my reflection stopped copying me.
I was filming a mirror trend. Hands up. Hair flip. Spin. I did it twice. On the third take, the reflection kept its arms down.

shots.prompt: large mirror in a dark bedroom reflecting a ring light and an empty room, no person

scenes.narration: I froze. I checked the real mirror. It copied me again. Perfectly. I laughed and blamed the lag.

shots.prompt: phone on a tripod facing a mirror, glowing screen, dark bedroom, no person

scenes.narration: Then I replayed the clip. My reflection was smiling. Not a normal smile. Too wide. Like it was waiting for me to notice.

shots.prompt: phone screen glowing in a dark room showing a blurry bright mirror, no text, no face

scenes.narration: I counted the seconds. At second nine, it looked past me. Straight into the camera. At whoever would watch this later.

shots.prompt: dark mirror with a ring light reflection, a pale blurred shape, no face

scenes.narration: I deleted the clip. My phone said it was still saving. Then it said posted. Nine hundred views. I never touched the button.

shots.prompt: phone lying on a bed, bright notification glow on the sheets, dark room, no text

scenes.narration: Every comment said the same thing. Turn around. Turn around. Turn around. I did not move. In the mirror, I did not move either.

shots.prompt: dark bedroom seen from behind a person in a hoodie facing a mirror, long shadows, no face

scenes.narration: Then my reflection lifted one hand and waved. I was holding the phone with both of mine.

shots.prompt: hand waving inside a dark mirror, cold blue light, no face

scenes.narration: I felt my mouth smile. I had not told it to.

shots.prompt: close view of a dark mirror edge with a faint smile-shaped reflection of light, no face

scenes.narration: So tell me. Do you cover the mirror, or keep filming?
